text:
maria: Heads-up: planning to publish tide-3b v1 to the model catalog tonight at 21:00 PT. Need someone to own the publish step + run the smoke checklist. Will also pin the alias for production traffic.

kyle: I can own the promote + post-publish smoke. I’ll be available 20:45–22:30 PT. :thumbsup:

sasha: I’ll prep the rollback artifact and monitor APM. Confirming: this is a straight model add, not replacing an existing production alias, right?

maria: Correct — it’s an additive model and we’ll create alias tide/latest -> tide-3b:v1 but won’t toggle traffic across any existing aliases.

dev-bot: CI check for tide-3b (v1) completed: unit tests ✅, integration tests ✅, eval harness ✅. checksum: a3f2b9c4

noah: Small ask: can we run the KV-cache warmup job after publish? New model has longer context mem, warmup reduces cold-latency spikes. I can queue it once publish is done.

kyle: Perfect — plan for the deploy: 1) upload weights to storage 2) register model metadata in catalog 3) create alias tide/latest pointing to tide-3b:v1 4) run smoke tests 5) if green, signal for warmup and metrics watch.

jenny: What are the smoke tests? Quick list so I can watch dashboards: inference smoke, latency p50/p95, token correctness on canonical prompts, cost sanity check.

maria: Exactly. Quick smoke commands I’ll run (for visibility):
```bash
# register model
redwoodctl model register --name tide-3b --version v1 --path s3://models/tide/3b/v1 --framework transformers
# publish to catalog
redwoodctl catalog publish --model tide-3b:v1 --visibility internal
# create alias
redwoodctl alias create --alias tide/latest --target tide-3b:v1
# run smoke suite
bin/smoke_inference.sh --model tide-3b:v1 --timeout 60
```

kyle: I’ll run those at 21:00 PT. I’ll post outputs here. If anything fails, immediate rollback is: alias delete tide/latest and catalog unpublish tide-3b:v1, plus a note to ops. Sasha will you take rollback if I call it?

sasha: Yep, I’ll execute rollback and open an incident channel if needed. I’ll also keep a snapshot of config and the previous alias state.

dev-bot: Deploy window reminder scheduled at 20:50 PT for channel eng-ml.

kyle: Starting publish now (21:00 PT). Upload step done. Registering model...

kyle: Register/logs: model registered id=mdl_8923, storage_checksum=a3f2b9c4

kyle: Catalog publish complete. Creating alias tide/latest -> tide-3b:v1

kyle: Alias created. Running smoke suite...

kyle: Smoke results:
```
SMOKE: inference_basic ... OK (rt 73ms)
SMOKE: long_prompt_consistency ... OK (p50 120ms, p95 310ms)
SMOKE: canonical_prompt_checks ... FAIL (1/15 mismatched tokens)
SMOKE: cost_sanity ... OK
```

jenny: Noted. Which canonical prompt failed? Might be tokenizer differences or a newline corner-case.

kyle: Failure log: sample id=42 mismatch at token 7, expected "," got "" (empty). Looks like a truncation at newline boundary. Pushing full logs to S3: s3://redwood-smoke-logs/tide-3b/v1/1815004321.log

noah: That could be a tokenizer config mismatch. Did the model registration include tokenizer config?

maria: Good catch — the registration step missed tokenizer.config in metadata. That can cause canonical diffs. We should unpublish alias until we fix. Sasha, go ahead with rollback.

sasha: Rolling back alias now. Alias tide/latest removed. Catalog entry unpublish queued.

dev-bot: Catalog unpublish job started for tide-3b:v1 (job id unpub-721).

kyle: Reverting and re-registering with tokenizer config included. Will re-run tests once updated. ETA 45m to re-run. Sorry for the noise — good catch team. :eyes:

maria: Thanks all. Action items: 
- kyle: re-register with tokenizer.config and re-run smoke (ETA ~45m)
- sasha: keep rollback steps ready and monitor infra
- noah: queue KV warmup after green
- jenny: keep dashboards open for p50/p95 and token mismatch metric

kyle: On it. Will post new thread if anything changes.

maria: Closing this thread for now; reopen once smoke passes. :rocket:
